title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Shortness of breath and productive cough.

Review of Systems:
ROS: Positive for cough, productive sputum, and fever. Denies chest pain, syncope, or lower extremity edema. Negative for sore throat, rhinorrhea, or abdominal pain.

Social History:
Lives in a private residence with her daughter. Retired. Non-smoker.

Family History:
Mother had hypertension. Father had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals (on admission):
T: 101.4 F, HR: 98, BP: 132/84, RR: 22, SpO2: 92% on RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 14.5K, Hgb: 11.8, Plt: 210K, BUN: 22, Cr: 1.1, Na: 138, K: 4.0.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 80-year-old female admitted with pneumonia. Initial presentation showed tachypnea and fever. Sputum culture was notable for MRSA. Started on IV vancomycin for infection. Pt responded well to antibiotics; fever resolved by day 3. Oxygen requirements decreased significantly. Transitioned to oral medications and cleared for discharge once stable and afebrile for 48 hours.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Pneumonia
- methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection

Discharge Medications:
- Vancomycin (completed)
- Amoxicillin 500mg BID x 7 days
- Acetaminophen 650mg PRN for fever/pain

Follow-up:
F/u with PCP in 1 week for wound check and respiratory status.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, MD, 05/18/2026
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09
